name: Photoelastic polariscope
summary: Stress made visible: a screen, one polariser sheet and a phone. The cheapest first real-world build. On paper.

inputs: the 1908 Brockhaus 'Licht' plate the author saved (figures 5 and 6: cooled and pressed glass)
outputs: the stress-optic law, its inversion and its assumptions

gate.condition: every assumption names a check that can fail

tools.name: CHECKS.json
tools.role: named check techniques the stage uses

law.name: stress-optic law (temporary birefringence)
law.form: delta = 2 pi t C (sigma1 - sigma2) / lambda; fringe order N = t (sigma1 - sigma2) / f_sigma, with f_sigma = lambda / C
law.lineage: Brewster (1816), stressed glass between polarisers; Maxwell (1853), the stress-optic relation; Coker and Filon, A Treatise on Photo-Elasticity (1931); Frocht, Photoelasticity (1941), the disc calibration; Michel-Levy (1888), the interference-colour chart

spec.quantity: principal stress difference sigma1 - sigma2 across a transparent part, and the principal directions
spec.signal: fringe order (isochromatics) and extinction bands (isoclinics) seen through crossed polarisers
spec.inversion: sigma1 - sigma2 = N f_sigma / t, with f_sigma measured on a calibration disc of the same sheet

wall_assumptions.assumption: the screen's light is linearly polarised
wall_assumptions.how_checked: rotate the analyser sheet over the white screen: near-black at one angle
wall_assumptions.if_broken: no fringes; use a second sheet as the polariser

wall_assumptions.assumption: the part is linear elastic and its fringes do not creep in time
wall_assumptions.how_checked: photograph at 10 s and 5 min under a fixed load; fringe order unchanged within 0.1
wall_assumptions.if_broken: photoviscoelastic: report time under load with every reading

wall_assumptions.assumption: residual (frozen-in) stress is known or subtracted
wall_assumptions.how_checked: photograph the unloaded part first; that image is the zero
wall_assumptions.if_broken: the moulding stresses of the Brockhaus figures, exactly; subtract the zero image

wall_assumptions.assumption: stress is uniform through the thickness (plane stress)
wall_assumptions.how_checked: thin flat parts only; thickness under a tenth of the in-plane size
wall_assumptions.if_broken: an integrated value, not a local one

wall_assumptions.assumption: the colour-to-order map holds for this screen and camera
wall_assumptions.how_checked: the stage-2 twin's map against the calibration disc, order by order
wall_assumptions.if_broken: count orders in single-colour light instead

spec.fundamental_bound: white-light colours wash out past about 4 to 5 orders (from memory, moderate); fringe-order resolution about 0.1 by colour, about 0.02 with phase stepping

stages.does_not_prove: Fringes give the difference of principal stresses, not each stress; separating them needs a second method.

inputs: the screen's spectrum and the camera's spectral response, each to be measured
outputs: a Jones-calculus twin: retardation to the RGB the camera records, for this screen

gate.condition: the twin's colour-to-order map recovers a planted retardation ramp within 0.1 order up to order 3

tools.name: tools/perceive
tools.role: perceptual bridge for the returned quantity

spec.model: plane and circular polariscope as Jones matrices; per wavelength, I = sin^2(2 theta) sin^2(delta / 2) (plane) or sin^2(delta / 2) (circular); integrate over the screen's spectral power times each camera channel's sensitivity
code: planned: polariscope/twin.py; the page's toy already runs the white-light case in the browser

noise_sources.name: camera shot and read noise
noise_sources.formula: sqrt(electrons) plus read noise per pixel
noise_sources.value: small next to colour ambiguity at these light levels

noise_sources.name: screen spectral lines
noise_sources.formula: three narrow primaries instead of a continuum
noise_sources.value: colours differ from the Michel-Levy chart; the twin fixes that

noise_sources.name: imperfect polarisers
noise_sources.value: unknown; measured as the dark level with no part

bounds.name: colour washout
bounds.formula: coherence of the source over the retardation

bounds.name: single-primary counting
bounds.formula: intensity sin^2(pi N) in one primary
bounds.value: dozens of orders countable, sign ambiguous

stages.does_not_prove: A twin built on measured spectra still assumes ideal sheets and no stray light.

outputs: the optical chain and its settings

gate.condition: extinction with crossed polarisers and no part: dark level below 2 percent of the open level in every channel

tools.name: phone camera in manual mode (fixed exposure, white balance, ISO)

chain.part_or_device: the screen itself, showing white, then pure green
clear polycarbonate parts (high sensitivity; acrylic shows few fringes)
one linear polariser sheet; circular: two pairs of cinema 3D glasses (each lens a linear polariser plus a quarter-wave film; from memory, moderate)

adc.enob_or_floor: the camera's RAW depth, 10 to 12 bits typical (from memory, low)

spec.margin_to_bound: colour is the limit; phase stepping with marked analyser angles buys about 5 times

stages.does_not_prove: One phone's colour pipeline is not another's; RAW avoids most of it.

outputs: a printed jig and a BOM of one sheet

tools.name: OpenSCAD
tools.role: printable load frame and disc holder

eda.tool: OpenSCAD for the jig; no circuit

alternates: polarised sunglasses (unknown axis; check over the screen)

spec.spend: gated: nothing ordered, priced or fabricated

stages.does_not_prove: A jig that fits proves nothing about the stress it applies.

outputs: capture and analysis code with self-tests

gate.condition: the dark-frame and zero-load tests run before every capture set

tools.name: OpenCV
tools.role: image registration and fringe tracing (R&D only; shipped code is ours)

toolchain.name: Python and NumPy; OpenCV only for R&D registration
toolchain.pinned: versions and code sha256 in each receipt

reproducible_build.check: same images give the same fringe map

self_tests.name: analytic specimen
self_tests.pass_condition: fringe pattern matches the closed-form field within 0.1 order

stages.does_not_prove: Passing self-tests says the optics and code behave, not that a part is safe.

outputs: f_sigma for this sheet, with its uncertainty

gate.condition: f_sigma from the disc and from the beam agree within their combined uncertainty

tools.name: CHECKS.json
tools.role: named check techniques the stage uses

spec.method: two specimens of one sheet. Disc of diameter D in diametral compression P: at the centre sigma1 - sigma2 = 8 P / (pi D t), so f_sigma = 8 P / (pi D N_centre) (Frocht). Beam in four-point bending: sigma = M y / I between the inner loads, fringes run parallel to the neutral axis with a linear order gradient

references.name: load from water bottles
references.traceability: volume times density (1 L of water near 0.998 kg at 20 C) or a kitchen scale of unknown calibration

references.name: ruler and calipers for D and t
closed-form disc and beam fields
references.traceability: elasticity theory: the shape of the field is exact; its scale rests on P, D and t

spec.honest_traceability: The fringe pattern's shape is a known answer from theory; its scale is only as good as a water bottle and a ruler. Readings say UNCAL until the disc and beam agree.

stages.does_not_prove: Two specimens from one sheet share its errors.

outputs: a screen-to-camera round trip with planted retardation

gate.condition: a planted retardation pattern shown on a second screen layer is read back within 0.1 order

spec.rig: digital to analog to digital: the screen displays the colours the twin predicts for a planted retardation map; the camera records them; the analysis must return the planted map. Then the physical disc under a known load closes the loop through real plastic

scoring.bits_lost: log2 of distinguishable orders before and after the camera, per pixel

stages.does_not_prove: A displayed planted map tests the camera and colour map, not the polariser sheets.

outputs: stress maps of real parts under a preregistered protocol

gate.condition: on 3 parts with a closed-form answer (disc, ring, notched beam) the mapped stress agrees within 15 percent

sites: plastic offcuts: disc, ring, notched beam
a clear plastic tree-tie or guard under its own clamp load (a real use)

protocol.prereg: a studyrun spec before the first field capture (not written yet)
protocol.kill_condition: median error above 15 percent on the known-answer parts
controls: the analyser rotated 90 degrees (fringes must invert)

stages.does_not_prove: Agreement on textbook shapes does not cover parts with complex 3D stress.

outputs: a receipt per part and load

tools.name: every-dimension bus.py
tools.role: receipt events on the measurement bus

tools.name: tools/perceive
tools.role: perceptual bridge for the returned quantity

spec.uncal_policy: UNCAL until the disc and beam calibrations agree; also when the zero-load image was not taken

feeds.findings: a FINDINGS entry when the field study runs

stages.does_not_prove: An image hash proves which photograph was read, not what stress the part held.

outputs: a kit: sheet, printed frame, calibration disc, analysis code

gate.condition: each kit's disc reads within 0.1 order of the reference kit's disc at the same load

design_for_test: each kit ships its own calibration disc
the dark-frame test runs on first use
spec.fixture: a reference load frame and one reference disc kept as the kit standard

yield.metric: share of kits whose disc passes

stages.does_not_prove: A kit standard is only a shared reference, not an absolute one.
